key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose where photoelectrochemical cells lose energy and translate those losses into concrete design choices for improving performance.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers compare device architectures, fit experimental J–V data, and prioritize optimizations such as co-catalysts, nanostructuring, and absorber selection.
method: Builds a single loss-analysis model for both BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes
Generates current-voltage curves, efficiency maps, and Sankey energy-flow diagrams
Fits experimental J–V data to decompose losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial terms
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation against state-of-the-art literature across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, including comparisons of Si, perovskites, hematite, and BiVO4.
watch_item: Because the framework relies on fitting experimental J–V data and idealized parameterization, its guidance may depend on data quality and how well real devices match the model assumptions.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
